source: Sources: Deseret News, Starlust (23 Nov 2026), ESA

scenes.vo: Getting to Mercury takes more energy than getting to Pluto. A probe just made it.
scenes.cap: Reaching Mercury took more energy than reaching Pluto

scenes.vo: On November twenty one, BepiColombo, from Europe and Japan, entered orbit around Mercury.
scenes.cap: 21 Nov: BepiColombo (ESA + JAXA) enters Mercury orbit

scenes.vo: Why so hard? Falling toward the Sun, you speed up. To get caught by tiny Mercury, you must slow down. A lot.
scenes.cap: Falling toward the Sun speeds you up. Mercury needs you SLOW.

scenes.vo: So it used planets as brakes. One flyby of Earth, two of Venus, and six of Mercury itself. Over eight years.
scenes.cap: Flybys: Earth x1, Venus x2, Mercury x6. Eight years.

scenes.vo: Only the second spacecraft ever to orbit Mercury. And it's two orbiters: ESA's MPO and Japan's Mio.
scenes.cap: Only the 2nd ever to orbit Mercury. Two orbiters: MPO + Mio

scenes.vo: One scare. The engine burn ran short, a software issue. ESA says the spacecraft is safe.
scenes.cap: Burn cut short by a software issue. ESA: spacecraft is safe

scenes.vo: They split in December. Science starts in April twenty twenty seven. Harder than Pluto. Worth it?
scenes.cap: They separate in December. Science starts April 2027.
